# Project Plan: Frac Pump Predictive Maintenance ("Fleet Reliability Command Center")

**Status:** v3.2 (after critique cycles 1-3; cycle 3 tie-out: 0 numeric mismatches, logic fixes applied) | **Owner:** Andrew Kraemer (SA) | **Date:** 2026-10-28
**Purpose:** FE Bar evaluation submission. One working end-to-end build plus a business deck.
**Numbers:** every figure below comes from `value_model/value_model_output.txt` (generated by `value_model.py`). Change log is in section 13.

---

## 0. One-paragraph pitch

Mesa Ridge Pressure Pumping (fictional) runs 15 dual-fuel frac fleets in the Permian: 300 active pumps and 60 standby. The modeled numbers:

- Unplanned pump failures cost an estimated **$11.9M a year**.
- Fluid ends, retired on a calendar, cost **~$61M a year**, its largest maintenance line.

The Fleet Reliability Command Center ingests pump telemetry, predicts which pump will fail and how within the next 24 pumping hours, prices the three options (keep running, swap at the next stage gap, pull now), and dispatches a technician. Run as a condition-based maintenance program, it's worth an estimated **$9.1-10.9M a year**. That's **$0.6-0.7M per fleet, or 3-4% of fleet EBITDA**:

- **$1.7-3.6M is directly ML-attributable** (failures caught early) and is proven in the POC backtest.
- **$7.3M comes from program levers** (fluid end life, consumables) that the same data enables and the pilot proves.

*All figures are modeled from public benchmarks; the POC replaces them with Mesa Ridge's CMMS, AP, and pump-hour data.*

## 2. Customer story and personas

**Company:** Mesa Ridge Pressure Pumping (fictional; name-checked before publishing). 15 dual-fuel fleets, Midland and Delaware. Each fleet has 20 active and 4 standby pumps, quintuplex, 2,500 HHP, stainless fluid ends.

| Persona | Role | Needs | KPIs with modeled baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dana Ortiz, VP Operations** (sponsor) | Signs the POC | EBITDA, fewer customer escalations, safety | EBITDA/fleet ~$18M; pump-caused NPT ~24 hrs/fleet/yr; ~279 unplanned repairs/yr (red-zone exposure) |
| **Marcus Lee, Director of Fleet Reliability** (owner) | Champion, owns the cost table and threshold | What to fix first, fewer surprises, longer fluid end life | Fluid end life 1,600 hrs; fluid end spend ~$4.1M/fleet; consumables ~$1.2M/fleet; MTBF (computed in gold from CMMS) |
| **Field service supervisor** | Daily user | Ranked list per stage gap, who's free, parts, work order | Work orders closed in window, MTTR |

**Demo storyline: the loud pump vs the expensive pump** (synthetic, scripted, labeled as such). Output from `decide_action()`:

| Rank | Pump | Mode, signal | Risk (24 hr) | Best action | Expected $ protected |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **F07-P09** | Power end bearing. Quiet: lube oil +9°F, crank LF vibration creeping | 0.72 | Pull now, standby online | **$48.7k** |
| 2 | **F07-P14** | Valve/seat washout. Loud: cylinder 3 valve impact energy rising | 0.86 | Swap at next stage gap | **$26.1k** |
| 3 | F03-P02 | Packing failure: packing temp rising, lube delivery dropping | 0.55 | Swap at next stage gap | $10.7k |

**Talking point:** the loud pump has the higher risk score, but the quiet pump is worth nearly twice as much. If a washout retires the whole fluid end (damage factor 1.0 instead of 0.4), F07-P14 jumps to $59k and ranks first. That's why Marcus owns the cost table and the POC calibrates it. The demo also shows **one miss and one false alarm**, with root cause for each.

## 3. Value model (single source of truth)

`value_model/value_model.py` is tagged SOURCED, ESTIMATE, or VALIDATE. It writes `value_assumptions.csv`, `mode_costs.csv`, and `value_model_output.txt`. The scoring job imports `decide_action()` from the same module, so the app, deck, and Genie can't disagree.

**Three levers**

| Lever | Mechanism | Measured in |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Failures caught early **(ML-attributable)** | The 24-hr failure-mode classifier flags valve/seat, packing, and power end failures, so the fix happens in a stage gap instead of a breakdown | POC backtest |
| 2. Fluid end life +10% (program) | The same telemetry flags **cavitation and operating-envelope abuse** (low suction at high HHP, pressure spikes). The suction-side fix extends fluid end life, the root cause behind Evolution's +63%. Analytics, not the classifier. **Accounting caveat:** if fluid ends are capitalized, this is capex/cash, not EBITDA, so confirm with the controller | Pilot |
| 3. Consumables -10% (program) | Valves, seats, and packing are replaced on condition, not hours (Baker Hughes: +27% valve life) | Pilot |

**Key outputs** (conservative = 25% caught at 50% precision; target = 50% at 35% precision, both points on the same threshold curve)

| | Conservative | Target |
|---|---|---|
| Unplanned events/yr (valve/seat 152, packing 82, power end 45) | 279 | 279 |
| Modeled cost of unplanned failures | $11.9M | $11.9M |
| Pump-caused spread NPT (24 hrs/fleet; deliberately conservative vs non-pumping time of 8-12%) | 362 hrs | 362 hrs |
| **Lever 1 (ML), net of false alarms + $0.6M run rate** | **$1.7M** | **$3.6M** |
| Lever 2, fluid end life | $5.5M | $5.5M |
| Lever 3, consumables | $1.8M | $1.8M |
| **Program total (steady-state, yr-1 implementation excluded)** | **$9.1M** | **$10.9M** |
| Per fleet / % of fleet EBITDA (ProPetro basis; higher on weaker-margin pumpers) | $0.60M / 3.4% | $0.73M / 4.0% |
| Lever 1 only, % of fleet EBITDA | 0.6% | 1.3% |
| EBITDA under any accounting (levers 1 + 3) | $3.5M | $5.4M |
| Spread hrs recovered (context only, not added to $) | 91 | 181 |
| False alarms per pump-month | 0.02 | 0.07 |
| Break-even precision ($37.4k avg net value per catch vs $4k per false alarm: standby swap + teardown inspection) | 9.7% | 9.7% |
| Payback, program (impl only / + $3M sensor allowance) | 1.0 / 5.0 months | 0.8 / 4.1 months |
| Payback, lever 1 only (impl only / + sensors) | 5.2 / 26 months | 2.5 / 13 months |

**Sensitivity:**

| Assumption | Range | Lever 1 or program result |
|---|---|---|
| Fluid end life extension | 5-20% | Program **$6.4-13.7M** (biggest swing) |
| Valve washout damage factor | 0.2-1.0 | Lever 1 $1.2-3.2M |
| Unplanned fluid end share | 10-35% | Lever 1 $0.8-2.3M |
| Power end rate | 0.05-0.25 | Lever 1 $1.2-2.3M |
| Share of failures that stop the spread | 0-100% | Lever 1 $1.4-2.1M |
| Consumables reduction | 5-20% | Program $8.2-10.9M |

**Validation rules (re-checked every iteration):**
1. Every number traces to `value_model_output.txt` or a cited source.
2. The conservative catch rate (25%) sits inside the analyst range (McKinsey 20-30% less unplanned downtime).
3. No double counting:
   - lost spread hours are valued once, at margin;
   - stages are context only;
   - cavitation is valued only in lever 2, not as a lever 1 event;
   - lever 1's fluid end damage is avoided early retirement from washouts (event-driven), while lever 2 is wear-driven life extension.
4. Headline numbers are marked "est."; the ML-attributable vs program split is always visible.
5. Forecast values say "expected" or "$ protected." "Saved" is reserved for realized outcomes, and the seeded realized outcomes are labeled synthetic.
6. Synthetic data calibrated to the value model is circular. It proves the pipeline works, not the value, and we say so.

## 5. Component specs

### 5.1 Names
- Workspace `fevm-production-forecasting` (profile `fe-vm-production-forecasting`); catalog `production_forecasting_catalog`; **schema `frac_pump_pdm`**; volume `raw_landing`
- Warehouse `6f1ac903576b114a`; LLM `databricks-claude-sonnet-4-6` (fallback `databricks-claude-haiku-4-5`)
- Lakebase Autoscaling project `frac-pump-pdm`, database `ops`; app `frac-reliability-center`
- Model `frac_pump_pdm.frac_pump_failure_model`; endpoint `frac-pump-failure-scorer`
- Bundle (`databricks.yml`) for the pipeline and jobs. The app deploys with the bundle, or with `databricks apps deploy`.

### 5.2 Synthetic data
| Dataset | Landing | Size |
|---|---|---|
| `fleets`, `pumps`, `technicians`, `parts_catalog`, `procedure_library` (synthetic OEM-style, labeled) | CSV/JSON | 15 / 360 / 60 / ~40 / ~12 |
| `telemetry_history`, months 1-11.9 | **Parquet** (historian export) | ~18M rows (300 pumps x 5,000 hrs x 12/hr) |
| `telemetry_live`, last 2 days | **JSON** edge messages, dripped by the replay job | ~0.1M rows |
| `stages` | CSV | ~43k |
| `maintenance_events` (CMMS) | CSV | ~940 fluid end changes + calendar valve changes + ~279 unplanned events |

**Telemetry fields (edge-computed):**
- `suction_psi`, `discharge_psi`, `pump_rpm`, `engine_load_pct`
- `theoretical_rate_bpm` (rpm x displacement; there's no per-pump flow meter on a manifold)
- `valve_impact_energy_c1..c5`, `valve_event_delay_ms_c1..c5` (crank-synced, computed at the edge from waveforms)
- `pe_vib_lf_rms`, `vib_kurtosis`, `pulsation_psi_pp`, `packing_temp_f`, `lube_oil_temp_f`, `lube_oil_psi`, `proppant_ppa`

The data dictionary marks which sensors are standard and which are an assumed retrofit.

**Realism:**
- Precursors per mode: valve/seat 2-10 hrs, packing 4-20 hrs, power end 20-100 hrs.
- Cavitation episodes come from low suction at high HHP and accelerate fluid end wear.
- Signals are normalized by rate and proppant.
- Calendar valve changes every 40-100 hrs are the counterfactual.
- Noise: false precursors, dropouts, ~10% ambiguous "unplanned" coding.
- **Seeded misses** have no precursor.
- Event counts are calibrated to the value model (calibration, not validation).

### 5.3 Lakeflow pipeline (SDP, serverless)
- **Bronze:** Auto Loader over Parquet + JSON + CSV, with `_rescued_data`.
- **Silver:** typed and deduped. Expectations: `discharge_psi BETWEEN 0 AND 15000` (drop), `pump_rpm >= 0` (drop), null-rate warnings.
- **Gold:**
  - `gold_pump_features` (hourly rolling 1/6/24 hr mean, slope, max; cylinder imbalance; hrs since last valve change; fluid end hrs)
  - `gold_failure_labels` (mode within the next 24 pumping hrs)
  - `gold_cavitation_flags` (suction below threshold at high HHP; feeds lever 2)
  - `gold_fleet_kpis_daily` (pump NPT, MTBF, maintenance $/stage)
- Evidence comes from an event-log query.

### 5.4 Unity Catalog governance
- Comments on all gold tables and columns, plus a `domain=reliability` tag.
- Column mask on `technicians.phone`. **The phone column is not synced to Lakebase or exposed in the app**, so the mask can't be bypassed.
- Grants: `reliability_analysts` get SELECT on gold; the app SP gets least privilege (see 5.11).
- Lineage from `system.access.table_lineage`, bronze onward. Volume to bronze comes from the pipeline definition; Lakebase to UC is proven by the R13 trace.
- *Stretch:* row filter by region.

### 5.5 ML (MLflow + UC)
- **Label:** `healthy | valve_seat_washout | packing_failure | power_end_bearing` within the next **24 pumping hrs (~3 stages)**. The model outputs a calibrated risk per mode, not a lead-time regression. Lead time is *measured* on true positives.
- **Split:** time-based. Train on months 1-9, test on months 10-12 (~70 events). Report n per mode and a 95% CI. Per-mode results are descriptive (power end n is about 11).
- **MLflow runs:** `calendar_baseline` (hours-since-change rule), `lightgbm_v1`, `lightgbm_v1_calibrated` (isotonic; Brier score + reliability table).
- **Metrics:**
  - event-level recall per mode, precision at threshold, false alarms per pump-month;
  - lead time P10 and median;
  - **annualized $ captured (x365/92) vs the calendar baseline**;
  - text artifacts: metrics table, confusion matrix CSV, gain importance.
- **Threshold:** maximize net $. `gold_threshold_curve` holds threshold, recall, precision, alarms/pump-month, and net $.
- **If the model doesn't beat the baseline:** report the gap honestly in evidence and the deck, and tune features once. No fudging the synthetic data after the fact.
- **Registry:** `@champion`. The promote step updates the endpoint to the same version, and the response includes `model_version`.

### 5.6 Ranked actions
The batch job calls `value_model.decide_action(risk, mode, standby_available)` per pump above threshold:
- keep running = `-risk x cost_if_failed`
- swap at next gap = `-planned_fix - risk x (hrs_to_gap / 24) x cost_if_failed` (requires a free standby pump)
- pull now = `-planned_fix - 0.75 hr x $/spread-hr x margin`
- `expected_savings = best - keep running`. This is a **one-time, per-decision** value. "$ protected this week" is the sum of `expected_savings` for work orders created that week.
- Each row exposes its inputs and `model_version`.

### 5.7 Lakebase
- **Phase 1 hard gate:** create the project; a triggered synced table (source with a PK + CDF); an OAuth write from a notebook; register the database as a UC catalog.
- **Fallbacks, decided now:**
  - (a) if synced tables fail, the scoring job writes `ranked_actions` directly to Lakebase with psycopg (still Lakebase serving);
  - (b) if UC registration fails, a job copies `work_orders` and `wo_events` to Delta for Genie.
- Synced: `pumps`, `pump_risk_latest`, `ranked_actions`. Native: `work_orders`, `technicians` (no phone), `tech_schedule`, `wo_events` (status plus realized-outcome fields; seeded history labeled `is_synthetic_seed`).
- "Re-score now" writes the new score to `pump_risk_latest_override` so the app never shows a stale score.

### 5.8 App (React + FastAPI, APX)
**Core:**
1. **Ranked Actions (hero):**
   - expected $ ranking with 3-option comparison per row;
   - drawer with sensor sparkline + drivers;
   - "Re-score now" (endpoint);
   - header KPIs: pumps at risk, $ at risk, model version.
2. **Dispatch and Timeline:** 48-hr Gantt across stage gaps. Assign, which creates a Lakebase work order, then track its status.
3. **AI Work Order** (modal from Dispatch):
   - grounded in `procedure_library` + `parts_catalog`;
   - cites the procedure ID and never invents torque or pressure values;
   - a human approves before save;
   - MLflow traced.
4. **Ask Genie** panel: Conversation API, showing SQL + result.

**Stretch (in order):** threshold panel from `gold_threshold_curve`, fleet overview tiles, row filter, what-if slider.

### 5.9 Genie Agent
- Sources: `gold_fleet_kpis_daily`, `gold_pump_risk_scores`, `gold_ranked_actions`, `maintenance_events`, `value_assumptions`, `mode_costs`, `work_orders` + `wo_events` (UC catalog or Delta copy), and metric view `mv_fleet_reliability` (MTBF, MTTR, pump NPT, maintenance $/stage, $ protected).
- Instructions: definitions, joins, "dollars come from value tables," and "expected vs realized; seeded = synthetic."
- 8 sample questions and 5 benchmarks.

### 5.10 End-to-end trace (R13 proof)
`scripts/trace_e2e.py` follows a single run:
1. drop a JSON file for F07-P09 into the volume;
2. pipeline update, bronze to gold row counts for that pump;
3. scoring job, risk + `model_version`;
4. Lakebase `ranked_actions` row;
5. app API `POST /work_orders`;
6. Lakebase `work_orders` row;
7. Genie answer that includes the new work order.

All output goes to `evidence/11_end_to_end_trace.txt`.

### 5.11 App service principal grants checklist
USE CATALOG/SCHEMA + SELECT on gold; CAN_USE on warehouse `6f1ac903576b114a`; CAN_QUERY on the serving endpoint and the FMAPI endpoint; CAN_RUN on the Genie Agent; Lakebase Postgres role with read on synced tables + read/write on native tables.

**Pre-agreed cut list if behind** (in this order): stretch items, then the "Re-score now" button (keep one endpoint curl), then the AI work order drops to a one-shot draft without approval, then Genie benchmarks drop to 3. **Never cut:** evidence export, the E2E trace, Lakebase writes, or the MLflow comparison.

**Repeated each phase:** (1) commit the evidence now; (2) does this make the $ story stronger or more credible? If not, cut it; (3) rerun `value_model.py` if an assumption moves; (4) log corrections in `tasks/lessons.md`.

## 8. Demo script (tell-show-tell, ~15 min, ~7 min live)
1. **Tell (2 min):** $9.1-10.9M on the table: $1.7-3.6M from the model, the rest from the program. What changes for Dana and for Marcus.
2. **Show (7 min):**
   1. Ranked Actions: the quiet power end (F07-P09, $48.7k, pull now) beats the loud valve (F07-P14, $26.1k, swap at gap).
   2. Drawer: precursor + drivers + the three options.
   3. "If washouts retire your fluid ends, the valve jumps to #1. That's your cost table, and we calibrate it together."
   4. Dispatch: AI work order (cites the procedure, human approves), assign to the 14:20 stage gap, and the timeline updates.
   5. Ask Genie: "Expected $ protected by this week's work orders, by fleet?"
   6. Under the hood (60 sec): pipeline, lineage, MLflow baseline vs model, Lakebase. Show one miss and one false alarm.
3. **Tell (3 min):** the value recap, then the POC with a week-1 data gate.

## 9. Top risks
| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Lakebase sync or UC registration fails | Phase 1 gate; fallbacks (a) and (b) in 5.7 |
| APX app + 5 integrations in one deploy | Grants checklist 5.11; build API routes against curl first, UI second; cut list |
| Model doesn't beat the calendar baseline | Honest-reporting path (5.5) |
| Synthetic metrics look too good | Noise, false precursors, seeded misses; targets: recall 50-70%, precision 35-50% |
| Buyer: "5-min data can't see valves" / "no per-pump flow" | Edge-computed crank-synced features; theoretical rate; POC verifies sensors |
| Endpoint cold start | Pre-warm; batch-score fallback |

## 12. FE Bar validator constraints (from go/fe-bar-faq, Oct 2026; see memory note)
- **The AI scorer reads at most 30 files, 9,000 chars each (the rest is truncated), and 90,000 chars total.** The planning docs alone are ~78k, so they move to `docs/` and the validator-facing layer is README + DECISIONS + evidence + deck, about 70k.
- **Evidence goes in `.md` files.** A Sept 2026 bug stripped .txt/.csv/.json/.log evidence. The README carries a master map (requirement to evidence file to what it proves), and the submission's decisions text box **names the evidence paths explicitly**.
- **Integrity checks:** commit authorship, plagiarism, prompt injection, Solution Builder detection. Commit per phase from the user's identity (the repo lives in `~/projects/0_db_public_repos/fe_bar` for the right credentials). `DECISIONS.md` documents the trade-offs and the AI-assisted workflow, since a "purely vibe-coded" build fails.
- **Four domains, all must be Meets or better:** Product, Industry, Build + AI Mindset, Customer Skills.
- **Roleplay (Yoodli):** a business persona + a technical persona, ~25 min hard limit. The demo must work live, and the candidate must close with next steps. `docs/roleplay_prep.md` turns the three critique cycles' toughest questions into prepared answers.
- `scripts/check_evidence.sh` fails if any validator-facing file is over 9k chars or the total is over 85k.
